The principle is to measure the absorption current of the capacitor due to a step voltage by an integrating method. The accuracy of measurement is expected to be a few PPM at 1 mHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of diodes used as precision power detectors above the square law region
abstract: The deviation from square law found in diode power detectors at moderate power levels has been modeled for a general system consisting of a number of diode detectors connected to a common arbitrary linear passive network, containing an approximately sinusoidal source. This situation covers the case of the six-port. The diodes are isolated from each other at DC. No assumption has been made about diode impedances, so that the diodes are interacting with the network as well as with each other at the fundamental frequency and at the harmonics. By applying the model the deviation can be eliminated if an extra-set of measurements is made in situ. For precision measurements the maximum power level can be increased by about 10 dB. The dynamic range can thus be increased sufficiently to enable fast measurements to be made with an accuracy of 10/sup -3/ dB.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experimental-theoretical approach to estimation of pulse propagation through ferrite filled waveguides
abstract: A method is developed for the analysis of the transient response of a ferrite-loaded waveguide in the time domain. The method is applicable to measurements of ferrite-loaded waveguides in the X-band. It is pointed out that the theoretical method and the numerical procedure developed may be adapted for a computerized network analyzer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CPEM '90 Digest. Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements (Cat. No.90CH2822-5)
abstract: Presents the front cover from the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: A magnetic-modulator-type current-dividing highly stable DC current transformer for large current
abstract: A highly stable current-dividing DC current transformer system using a second-harmonic type of magnetic modulator has been developed for a several-hundred-ampere highly regulated current source which is required for nuclear magnetic resonance measurements. The system consists of a resistive current divider, two choke coils, and two magnetic modulator ampere-turn comparators, using relatively small cores, with feedback. The performance of the regulated current source was tested by setting the current supply to 200 A. A temperature drift of 3 p.p.m./ degrees C in the regulated output current was achieved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An adaptive method for automatic calibration of interpolation time interval digitizer with picosecond resolution
abstract: An adaptive method is presented for real-time calibration of an interpolation time-interval digitizer (TID) with picosecond resolution. Reduction of calibration uncertainty to the level of 3 ps (RMS) has been achieved. Experimental results and comparison with some existing methods for TID calibration are also presented. The adaptive method was developed to solve a calibration problem that emerged in the course of developing an advanced TID for a satellite laser ranging systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Establishment of Josephson array voltage standard system at KSRI
abstract: A Josephson array voltage standard system that is used to maintain the national standard of voltage in Korea according to the CIPM recommendation is described. The standard, which consists of a microwave source, electronics, and a cryogenic unit was constructed using a 2076-junction array. Measurement shows that the mean value of EMF of the primary standard cell group differs from the expected value by 9.8 p.p.m. if the new Josephson constant, K/sub J-90/ =483597.9 GHz/V, is used to calculate the array voltage. The difference originates mainly from the use of a different value of K/sub J/, and the resultant change of EMF of the cells is less than 0.6 p.p.m. in ten years.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coherent fiber optic reflectometer
abstract: A novel method for measuring the reflection of fiber-optic devices with light carrier frequency dependence such as fiber resonators is proposed. and the design of an experiment based on the proposed principle is described. Results of the measurement of the power transmission and power reflection coefficients of a 20-cm Fabry-Perot-type fiber resonator are presented. It is concluded that the proposed method can provide a precise measurement of the reflection of fiber resonators.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A set of improved signal processing algorithms and their application in measuring alternating electrical parameters by synchronous sampling
abstract: The author proposes a set of improved signal processing algorithms which are based on linear interpolation and are suitable for the measurement of alternating electrical parameters. Theoretical analyses and experiment results show that, if time deviation is within one sample interval, the improved algorithms can diminish the truncation errors greatly without using additional hardware, whereas the traditional algorithms probably cause intolerable errors because they are unable to reflect the signal distribution properly in a signal period.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Circuit precautions for stable operation of Josephson junction array voltage standard
abstract: Steps taken during the course of developing a Josephson junction array voltage standard to achieve a measurement uncertainty of better than 2*10/sup -8/ are described. They consist of improving the frequency stability of the Gunn oscillator by proper design of the phase-locked loop, choosing a digital voltmeter (DVM) with high resolution, low drift, and low noise emission for use as a null detector, and designing line filters to reduce noises introduced into the Josephson junction array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement of resistance ratios in the range to 100 megohms
abstract: The results of using a technique of potentiometrically comparing the voltage drops across two resistors in series utilizing an automatic potentiometer are presented. It is shown that a source voltage of 10 V is adequate to make 1:1 ratio resistance measurements from 10/sup 3/ Omega to 10/sup 8/ Omega to within +or-0.5*10/sup -6/. The same source voltage of 10 V can be used to make 10:1 ratio measurements from 10/sup 3//10/sup 2/ Omega to 10/sup 8//10/sup 7/ Omega to within +or-1*10/sup -6/. The source voltage of 10 V can also be used to make 100:1 ratio measurements from 10/sup 5//10/sup 3/ Omega to 10/sup 8//10/sup 6/ Omega to within +or-6*10/sup -6/. Ratios of 1:10 can also be measured. but in general the anticipated uncertainty is some 2-5 times greater than when a 10:1 ratio is measured.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Monitoring the mass standard: a comparison of mechanical to electrical power
abstract: An ongoing absolute watt experiment that shows the promise of being able to monitor the stability of the kilogram standard to better than 0.05 p.p.m. is discussed. The theory is presented, and the latest improvements to the experimental apparatus are briefly described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Magnetic field sensor for measurements of transients
abstract: The basic principles, design, and testing of a magnetic field sensor based on an electrically small loop are reported. A sensor comprising a single-turn loop, current transformer, and broadband amplifier was modeled using the SPICE simulation program. A sensor was designed to operate from approximately 5 kHz to 100 MHz. It consists of a square loop with a total length of 24 cm and a wire diameter of 1.3 mm. The ferrite transformer has mu =850, n=25. The computer simulation and test results are presented and are in good agreement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The progression of ratio measurement and technique
abstract: Progress in three areas in the field of ratio measurement and techniques is reviewed. These areas are the splitting and interleaved winding inductive voltage divider and voltage transformer, the impedance incrementary ratio arm bridge, and the generalized self-calibration method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An adaptive internal calibration of a voltage calibrator
abstract: An algorithm for adaptive internal calibration of a precision voltage calibrator is discussed. Due to the built-in metrology organization and real-time data processing of measurement results, improved traceability is obtained. An evaluation of internal calibration results indicates that a learning control algorithm is feasible, thus extending the normal calibration recall cycle.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PTB-NIST bilateral comparison of microwave noise power in coaxial transmission line
abstract: The Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt and the National Institute of Standards and Technology have compared microwave noise power in coaxial transmission lines. Each laboratory measured two solid-state noise sources at 2.0 GHz, 4.0 GHz, and 8.0 GHz relative to their primary thermal noise standards. The agreement between laboratories is better than 0.07 dB, which is within the stated uncertainties of the two services, namely +or-0.06 dB for NIST, and +or-0.04 dB for PTB (confidence level: 0.95).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved technique and standard resistors for the measurement of high value resistances
abstract: A description is given of an adapted Wheatstone bridge measurement system based on the balanced-bridge method, which has been automated for the comparison of high-value resistance standards between 10/sup 8/ Omega and 10/sup 14/ Omega . The system has been tested with high-magnitude standard resistors. The relative measurement uncertainty of the system for the comparison of two 5*10/sup 8/- Omega resistors was found to be smaller than 1*10/sup -6/, which is about a factor of five better than values obtained with other systems. This value increases for bridge ratios of 1:10 and 1:100 at higher resistances to about 2*10/sup -5/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A broadband radiometer for calibrating mismatched noise sources
abstract: The accurate modeling of the effect of source match on receiver noise is reported. This makes it possible for mismatched noise sources to be calibrated accurately with neither isolators nor tuners. The broadband radiometer used for the calibration is briefly described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measuring thickness of a thin film conductor using solenoid coil
abstract: A method for accurately estimating the thickness of a paramagnetic film conductor from the difference in the complex impedance between a circular solenoid coil equipped with a conductor and a similar one without a conductor has been studied. For aluminum films with a thickness of 15 to 60 mu m in a frequency range of 10 to 500 kHz, the discrepancy between the measured values using this method and those using a micrometer stayed within 3%.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of measurement bandwidth on time domain device modeling
abstract: The effect of the measurement system bandwidth on the time-domain modeling of microwave devices is investigated. The modeling is performed in the time domain using the modified transient circuit analysis package (MTCAP) together with TDR (time-domain reflectometry) waveforms experimentally measured for the device. Depending on the transition duration (rise time) of the TDR system, the details obtained on the TDR waveforms and consequently the complexity of the obtained model vary accordingly. It is shown that, with a faster TDR system, the modeling process is more difficult and the number of components in the equivalent circuit is increased. However, this equivalent network model gives a better characterization of the microwave device under test.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calculation of the Shapiro step amplitudes in two-dimensional Josephson tunnel junctions (voltage standard)
abstract: The amplitudes of RF-induced constant voltage steps in two-dimensional Josephson tunnel junctions is investigated theoretically using a first-order approximation of the current density distributions in the junction. A planar resonator model is used to analyze the electromagnetic field in the microwave-driven junction. It is found that the power dependence of the Shapiro step height in two-dimensional resonant junctions is different from that in one-dimensional junctions. The maximum amplitude is lower, and the microwave amplitude, which is needed to reach the maximum step height, is increased. The step amplitude oscillates with increasing power, but it does not reach zero. The smooth curve of the step amplitude near its maximum gives a wide microwave power region of sufficiently high step amplitudes in two-dimensional junctions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High precision comparison of quantized Hall resistances
abstract: Relative values of quantized Hall resistances R/sub H/(i) have been measured on the plateaus of i=4 and 2 for a GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure device under the complete quantization condition and compared with each other. The value of 4*R/sub H/(4) differs appreciably from the value of 2*R/sub H/(2). This result suggests a possible deviation of i*R/sub H/(i) from the universal value h/e/sup 2/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new test of relativity using hydrogen maser standards
abstract: A novel test of relativity that was performed using advanced time and frequency technology of the Deep Space Network is discussed. The instrumentation, procedure. and data analyses are described. By directly measuring the propagation-delay variation between two masers, limits on a possible anisotropy in the one-way velocity of light have been obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sub-PPM linearity testing of a DMM using a Josephson array
abstract: The design and operation of a system that uses a 10-V Josephson array to measure automatically the linearity of precision digital multimeters (DMMs) are described. Software automatically sets the array voltage to appropriate levels over the range of interest, controls the data collection at each data point, performs data reduction, and stores the data on disk for archival and future recall. The results reported demonstrate the ability of the system to measure the linearity more accurately than 0.1 p.p.m. of 10 V. Tests on some DMMs demonstrated peak linearity errors as small as 0.03 p.p.m.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A precision thermal wattmeter having a sampling control system and an analogue feedback loop
abstract: A precision thermal wattmeter having a sampling control system and an analog feedback loop is described. A pair of thermal converters is used as a sum and difference multiplier and as an AC/DC power comparator simultaneously. The large error caused by insufficient open-loop gain in the wattmeter is removed by the sampling control system. The wattmeter is designed for use at relatively low frequency. The maximum sensitivity is better than 1 p.p.m., and total accuracy is estimated at better than 20 p.p.m.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interferometric measurement with external modulation and recycling: theory and verification
abstract: A novel modulation technique for the shot-noise-limited measurement of the different displacement between arms of a Michelson interferometer is presented. Electrooptic modulation is applied to a reference beam external to the Michelson system, avoiding modulator-induced losses and wavefront distortions and allowing efficient power increase through recycled-light operation. Results for initial proof-of-concept experiments are given and show reasonable agreement with theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A combined X-ray and optical interferometer with a new translation stage
abstract: A novel translation stage with an 80- mu m stroke has been made for the measurement of silicon

articleTitle: A new microcalorimeter in K/sub a/ band
abstract: Based on an analysis of a thermistor mount which is used as the load of a microcalorimeter, a novel type of K/sub a/-band microcalorimeter is reported. The total uncertainty of the microcalorimeter in calibrating directly the effective efficiency eta /sub e/ of commercial thermistor mounts has been estimated to be +or-0.2 to +or-0.5%.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A W-band homodyne vector network analyzer without mechanical signal reversing switch
abstract: A low-cost homodyne vector network analyzer for use from 90 to 100 GHz is presented. The waveguide setup consists of two identical measurement heads that can be moved relative to each other. The millimeter-wave signal is fed to the moving head through a novel quasi-optical line stretcher. A calibration procedure that has been developed for this setup is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An efficient six-port procedure for power meter calibration
abstract: A method for the efficient calibration of a single six-port network used to measure both the effective efficiency and the calibration factor of a power meter is presented. An automated 2-18-GHz implementation and the validation of the method are described. The junction is based on a design using four quadrature hybrids, with the forward and reflected waves sampled using 3-dB and 10-dB couplers, respectively. Because there is no need to tune the test port to a match at each frequency, the presence of a maladjusted lossless tuner between the test port and the power meter should not affect the value obtained for the effective efficiency, although the calibration factor will vary. This concept has been used to test the system by measuring the effective efficiency and calibration factor of a combined tuner and power meter at one frequency. The results demonstrate that the measured effective efficiency is constant to within 0.1% for reflection coefficients up to 0.2.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An accurate 10 k Omega resistance standard
abstract: The design and performance of six 10-k Omega standard resistors fitted in thermoregulated enclosures are described. A potentiometric resistance comparator was used to compare the six resistors among themselves. The resistance values, known in terms of a quantized Hall resistance standard, were found to drift at constant rates ranging from six to 64 parts in 10/sup 9/ per year. The results show that the resistance values can be predicted, over periods of months, to one part in 10/sup 8/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quantum Hall samples prepared by helium-ion implantation
abstract: GaAs/GaAlAs heterostructure-based quantum Hall samples with a wide range of electron mobilities have been produced using ion implantation. The purpose was to optimize the samples for use in metrology. In particular, the critical current and the nonohmic behavior of the samples in the vicinity of a quantum Hall plateau were studied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Superdeep frequency division as a new principle for designing a standard of phase shift angle between two electrical signals for the frequency range of 1 kHz to 30 MHz
abstract: The authors present a novel principle for the reproduction of the phase-shift angle (PSA) between two electrical signals (voltages, currents, etc.) in a wide frequency range. This approach enables one to specify angles with a discreteness of 0.001-0.0001 degrees a at frequencies of 100 kHz and 1, 10, 20, and 30 MHz within the angle range of 0-360 degrees . The principle is based on the method of superdeep frequency division in two channels (by a factor of 10/sup 7/-10/sup 8/) in a decade structure of direct frequency synthesis. The basic theoretical relations of the method, calculations for the preferred variant, and an experimental error study are presented. In the USSR, this principle was used to design the state PSA standard for the frequency range of 10/sup -2/ Hz to 30 MHz with the PSA range of 0-360 degrees in 1988.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Millimeter wave (MMW) time domain automatic network analysis techniques
abstract: A possible scheme of MMW time-domain automatic network analysis (TDANA) is presented, and its principle is demonstrated mathematically. The transfer characteristics of a bandpass filter with central frequency of 35 GHz and passband width of 1 GHz were measured. With a frequency resolution of 50 MHz and a dynamic range of 35 dB, the random uncertainties of amplitude and phase in the passband are within 0.15 dB RMS and 4 degrees RMS, respectively. The experimental results show that the scheme and the principle introduced are valid and can be widely used in the analysis of linear network characteristics in the MMW region.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A performance evaluation of an RF switching radiometer
abstract: The authors present a performance evaluation of an RF switching radiometer used as a noise comparator at X-band. The sensitivity, thermal stability, and noise source stability are examined. The temperature stability was improved by circulating water on the critical components. The system is sufficiently sensitive and stable for the calibration of noise sources. The precision of the noise temperature measurement is estimated within 0.01 dB using a gas-discharge standard noise source.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach to 'TRL' calibration for dual six-ports and network analysers
abstract: Dual six-ports, and other network analyzers that can be treated as mathematically equivalent to dual vector four-ports, are commonly calibrated by the TRL (through-reflect-line) method or one of its variants. The use of unknown one-ports for calibration with this method, and also for super-through-short-delay, an extension of the TRL method. is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An automated 60 GHz open resonator system for precision measurement of loss tangent and permittivity
abstract: A Fabry-Perot hemispherical open resonator system has been designed and constructed for precision measurement of loss tangent and dielectric permittivity of low absorbing materials at 60 GHz. The resonator system uses a cavity made with optically polished copper spherical and flat mirrors, highly stabilized synthesized phase-locked Gunn oscillator sources, and a superheterodyne receiver to enable measurement of loss tangent values as low as 10 mu rad. Using this system, the real part of the dielectric permittivity can be measured with an accuracy almost as high as that achieved with dispersive Fourier transform spectroscopy. A block diagram of the complete measurement system is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characteristics of a frequency stabilized and spectral narrowed laser diode system
abstract: Frequency-stabilized and spectral-linewidth-narrowed laser diode systems are being developed for optical pumping of a cesium atomic clock. Frequency stabilization and reduction of spectral linewidth were carried out by utilizing optical feedback from a Fabry-Perot interferometer. Saturation absorption and fluorescence spectroscopy results are presented. It is shown that the long-term stability of optical locking is not sufficient for a practical atomic clock.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Increasing the time-constant of a thin film multijunction thermal converter for low frequency application (AC/DC transfer)
abstract: A planar thin-film multijunction thermal converter (MJTC) developed for low-frequency application has been optimized by adding a thermal mass in the heater area to increase the time constant of the MJTC from 100 ms to 3 s and more. The thermal mass of silicon is left under the heater during the anisotropic etching process. This technique should substantially reduce the transfer difference at frequencies below 100 Hz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of a new audio-frequency power bridge
abstract: Several techniques for measuring active and reactive power in the 50-Hz to 20-kHz frequency range are described. These approaches were developed to evaluate a new high-accuracy, audio-frequency power bridge that is based on AC voltage and impedance measurements. The results indicate that its uncertainties are within the expected +or-200 p.p.m. for active power. The bridge and a high-precision sampling wattmeter constructed using two sampling digital voltmeters are described. A dual-channel digitally synthesized source was used to verify measurements at zero power factor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An electronically enhanced magnetic core for current transformers
abstract: Summary form only given. An electronic technique which greatly increases the apparent permeability of a magnetic core of a current transformer without a galvanic connection to either of the usual primary or secondary winding circuits is described. The number of turns and the turns ratio can be selected independently as desired. Means are available for examining the waveform of the magnetizing current for the presence of even harmonics, thus indicating possible remanence or direct currents in the windings. Application of the technique to transformer voltage dividers is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization and modeling of a wideband microstrip balun
abstract: The authors describe the characterization and modeling of a hybrid microwave balun with a wide frequency bandwidth from near DC to about 5 GHz. The modeling is carried out in the time domain by using the modified transient circuit analysis package (MTCAP) and the PSPICE package in the frequency domain for verification purposes. The phase-reversal transition region is shown to limit the balun's bandwidth. The effect of the ground current due to phase reverse can be modeled using a high-impedance transmission line coupled with a negative signal line at the phase-reversal junction. The model obtained is in good agreement with experimental results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparison of sensitivity to location errors in mathematical transformation of arbitrary electromagnetic fields
abstract: A comparison is made of three methods of mathematically transforming arbitrary electromagnetic fields from measurements of the power spectral density made in the near field: the point matching method, the diffraction method, and the random mode method. The methods are compared in terms of sensitivity to location errors, storage, and computational requirements. The results are verified by a computer simulation of an arbitrary source.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New low-voltage standards in the DC to 1 MHz frequency range
abstract: Several techniques for measuring the RMS value of 1-600-mV signals are described and compared to existing thermal transfer standards. Differences between the techniques at 100 mV are typically within +or-20 p.p.m. in the audio-frequency range and within +or-100 p.p.m. out to 1 MHz. A new low-voltage thermal transfer standard has made it possible to compare thermal converters, micropotentiometers, and a digitally synthesized source to a precision of 1 p.p.m. The results indicate that micropotentiometers, are inherently more accurate transfer devices in the DC to 1-MHz frequency range than low-voltage TVCs (thermal voltage converters).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of new hydrogen masers at the National Research Council of Canada
abstract: Two active hydrogen masers designed to be operated as clocks and as contributors to the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) time scale have been constructed. Details of their design are presented together with some initial measurements of line-Q and frequency stability. A plot of maser power as a function of linewidth for maser H4 is shown. The experimental values of linewidth at the extremes of the oscillation curve correspond to line-Q values of 6.1*10/sup 9/ and 1.3*10/sup 9/, respectively. At a reasonable operating atom flux, the line-Q is 4*10/sup 9/, which is a factor of two better than that obtained for maser H1 at its normal operating flux. Some initial measurements of the frequency stability of the masers have also been made.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cryogenic Fabry-Perot interferometer for time, gravity and material property experiments
abstract: A Fabry-Perot interferometer to operate at cryogenic temperatures is discussed. The following possible applications of this device are discussed: stabilization of a laser and precise time measurements; measurements of the change in energy of a resonant multimode gravitational wave detector; and measurements of the expansion coefficient of materials at low temperatures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Physical nature and exact definition of electric power
abstract: The physical nature has been determined and exact definitions found for various kinds of electric power occurring in electrical circuits. Both the components of energy and power and the characteristic parameters are convenient to instrument in the time domain. With these components and parameters, a comprehensive evaluation of the entire source-load system, such as the reciprocal flow of energy between source and load and/or within the load, the local concentration of power, the shift-deformation of waveforms, etc., can be correctly obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigating the use of multimeters to measure quantized Hall resistance standards
abstract: A new generation of digital multimeters was used to compare the ratios of the resistances of wire-wound reference resistors and quantized Hall resistances (QHRs). Specifically, a digital multimeter was used to compare the DC voltage ratio of a QHR sample with that of a reference resistor connected in series with the sample. The accuracies are better than 0.1 p.p.m. for ratios as large as 4:1 if the multimeters are calibrated with a Josephson array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The representation of the ohm using the quantum Hall effect at IEN
abstract: A method to measure the quantized Hall resistance (QHR) in terms of the Istituto Elettrotecnico Nazionale (IEN), Italy, reference standard is described. Measurements showing the independence of QHR from the experimental conditions are reported. A preliminary evaluation of the difference between Omega /sub IEN/ and the new quantum-Hall-based standard is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of noise and bandwidth on homomorphic deconvolution
abstract: The impulse response of an unknown system is recovered from time-domain reflectometry (TDR) data using the homomorphic deconvolution technique. TDR waveforms obtained from the simulation of resistive and reactive discontinuities are used to investigate the effect of the system's bandwidth on the homomorphic deconvolution. The effects of the noise content in the processed waveforms as well as the system's bandwidth on the deconvolution process are studied. The same deconvolution applications are also treated using the optimal compensation deconvolution method, and the results are compared. The homomorphic deconvolution technique is shown to be fairly sensitive to the noise content in the TDR waveform. For an SNR (signal-to-noise ratio) of less than 40 dB, the cepstrum becomes very noisy, and the separation of the convolution components is not practical. It is concluded that noise reduction techniques are needed to improve the SNR, thus enabling the use of the homomorphic deconvolution technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Beam shaping of radiation pattern of H-sectoral horn loaded with ferrite
abstract: The partial loading of the apertures of H-sectoral horns with magnetized ferrite strips is reported. A pair of thin ferrite strips are placed symmetrically on the aperture of the horn. The ferrite strips are magnetized transverse to the direction of propagation. Radiation pattern measurements were performed at 10 GHz, and beam sharpening and beam skewing are observed. These effects are due to the tensorial nature of the permeability of the magnetized ferrite. Comparison of theoretical and experimental patterns shows good agreement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A computerized model of vacuum thermocouple performance
abstract: Heat-flow equations for a simplified vacuum thermocouple (VTC) were computerized using a Crank-Nicholson two-step finite-difference scheme. Comparisons were made between the computer outputs and measured values for both 500-mA and 5-mA VTCs. Curve-shape studies, radiation losses, conduction losses through all imperfect vacuum, and thermal conductivity considerations are discussed. The steady-state case demonstrated strong dependence of thermal conductivity on temperature. The output performance characteristics of the 500-mA VTC are controlled principally by the thermal conductivity of the heater, whereas those of the 5-mA units are dominated by thermal conductivity of the thermocouple wire. Calculations show that, even for very low emissivity coefficients, radiation losses are substantial in the 5-mA type, which are commonly used for AC-DC transfer standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Diode laser-pumped Rb-beam atomic clock as a novel primary frequency standard
abstract: A laser-pumped rubidium-beam atomic clock is proposed to improve the accuracy of the clock's microwave frequency and to develop a novel primary frequency standard. In this system, the clock is controlled by using the optical-microwave double-resonant signal. Several preliminary experiments were carried out. In the first step, the authors observed the fluorescence signal of pumped atoms in the Rb beam and confirmed the effect of optical pumping. In the second step, approximately 1 kHz of linewidth was obtained in the derivative of the microwave resonant signal.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement of complex RMS value of the fundamental harmonic under nonsinusoidal conditions
abstract: Two algorithms for calculating the complex RMS values of the voltage and current fundamental harmonics in the presence of harmonic distortion are given. One is based on direct calculation of the discrete Fourier transform and the other on cyclic convolution. It is shown that the algorithms reduce the number of multiplications needed to approximately one multiplication per one eliminated harmonic and need three times as many additions. at a relatively low sample rate. Therefore. the algorithms are useful for real-time applications. It is shown how to evaluate the aliasing errors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An experiment in X-ray interferometry: accuracy and resolution in Si d/sub 220/ determination
abstract: The authors analyze the resolution and the accuracy obtained in an experiment carried out to measure the silicon lattice spacing with scanning X-ray interferometry equipment. This study was prompted by the observation of a discrepancy in comparing results obtained by the authors with those obtained by other research groups. With the previous apparatus used by the authors, compensation and correction for systematic errors required considerable effort during interferometer coupling and experiment execution. With the use of a new X-ray/optical interferometer, cosine and Abbe's errors are expected to remain below 10/sup -7/, even if, in the worst case, trajectory misalignment and offset occur. Contribution to the error budget of the crystal temperature and diffraction effects in the optical interferometer have also been considered and reduced to acceptable levels. Experimental tests and a theoretical analysis show that improvements are possible and that the desired accuracy can be obtained. A new set of lattice spacing measurements with the new apparatus is being carried out to reduce the overall uncertainty to a few parts in 10/sup -8/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Laser diode optically pumped cesium beam frequency standard investigations at LHA
abstract: Summary form only given. Investigations of the laser-diode optically pumped cesium beam resonator are discussed. The basic atomic resonator operates with a switched-capacitor laser diode tuned to either the D/sub 1/ or D/sub 2/ cesium line at 894 and 852 nm, respectively. The optical transitions that give the highest clock signal amplitude are found to be sensitive to the Hanle effect. The optical pumping efficiency as well as the fluorescence yield decrease when the static magnetic field is too low in the light atom interaction regions. An efficient optically pumped cesium beam resonator having three magnetic field regions has been designed. When it operates with a commercially available laser diode tuned on the 3 to 3 sigma transition at 852 nm, it exhibits an S/N ratio=2*10/sup 4/ in 1-Hz bandwidth, leading to a measured short-term frequency stability of 2*10/sup -12// square root tau . The influence of the anisotropic character of the fluorescence light on the collection efficiency of the fluorescence light in the detection region has also been investigated. Preliminary investigations of the statistical properties of the fluorescence signal and their dependence on the different noise sources have been carried out.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Properties of alloyed AuGeNi-contacts on GaAs/GaAlAs-heterostructures
abstract: The technique of contacting GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures using an evaporated AuGeNi alloy has been refined with emphasis on optimum contact properties in the quantum Hall regime. The resistance of the electrical contacts to two-dimensional electron gas has been measured in various heterostructures with two different methods. The results of the first method using a transmission line and the second one using the quantum Hall effect as well as the good time and thermal cycling stabilities obtained demonstrate the high quality of the contacts. The contact resistance in the quantum Hall regime is found to be lower than 1 Omega .<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurements of the quantized Hall resistance at the ETL
abstract: The quantized Hall resistance R/sub H/(4) of Si-MOSFETs has been measured in terms of Omega /sub ETL/ by the use of a recently constructed measurement system at the Electrotechnical Laboratory, Japan. The time variation of the 1- Omega /sub ETL/ resistance standard relative to the QHR is traced. A potentiometric method is used to compare R/sub H/(4) with a reference resistor of nominal value 6453.2- Omega . A cryogenic current comparator system is used to link the 6453.2- Omega resistor to Omega /sub ETL/. The estimated overall uncertainty is 5*10/sup -8/. The experimental equipment and procedure are described in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the theoretical curves of site attenuations at frequencies below 80 MHz
abstract: The site attenuations of open-area test site are calculated by the method of electromotive force, and the cause of a characteristic hump in the site attenuation curve below 80 MHz is explained. The deviation between the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) site attenuations and the experimental results on an ideal open area test site at these frequencies was found to be due to the mutual coupling effects of the antennas under the FCC's measurement conditions. Therefore, it is recommended that the theoretical site attenuation curves below 80 MHz given by FCC's OET-55 measurement conditions be revised.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High precision range extenders for an AC calibrator up to 600 V and 100 A
abstract: Summary form only given. The development of high-precision range extenders for high voltage (600 V) and large current (100 A) as separate units to be used with a previously developed AC calibrator is discussed. To obtain high accuracy and stable operation, an error feedforward technique was implemented. A current-comparator-based capacitance bridge was used for the gain, and phase calibration of the range extender. A precision two-stage current transformer and a very stable time-division-based watt-converter were used to verify its performances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a GPS time comparison system and the GPS common-view measurements
abstract: An L1 band (1575.42 MHz), C/A (coarse/acquisition) code GPS receiver for precise time comparisons has been developed. GPS measurements in common-view have been carried out between the Korea Standards Research Institute (KSRI) and the Communications Research Laboratory (CRL), Japan. The frequency stability of the KSRI master clock has been measured against the master clock of CRL for 50 d. The frequency stability is about 1 part in 10/sup 13/ for the averaging time of 4 d.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Selection of the starting sampling point of periodic signals
abstract: In quasi-integer-period sampling, the error of the average value derived from the sampling data is different for different processing methods. However, proper selection of the starting sampling point can reduce this error significantly. The problem is studied more thoroughly in the frequency domain, and it is shown to what extent this error can be diminished and what the residual error is.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 303-MHz frequency standard based on trapped Be/sup +/ ions
abstract: A 303-MHz hyperfine transition in the ground state of Be/sup +/ ions stored in a Penning trap was used as the basis for a frequency standard. Linewidths as narrow as 900 mu Hz were obtained. The inaccuracy in the second-order Doppler shift was reduced to 5 parts in 10/sup 15/ by laser cooling.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A single trapped strontium ion: a first step towards an improved frequency standard
abstract: Summary form only given. Current progress at the National Research Council of Canada toward a practical frequency standard based on a single trapped strontium ion is discussed. It is pointed out that a single Sr/sup +/ ion is an excellent compromise for a first-generation single-ion frequency standard. Its transition rate, 2.7/s, is fast enough for good data to be obtained in moderate experimental periods. yet slow enough to allow an unsophisticated microcomputer programmed in BASIC to keep up with it and slow enough that the natural linewidth. 0.4 Hz in 445 THz, permits a precision exceeding that of cesium standards. The experimental design is described in some details.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Precision measurements using laser cooled atoms
abstract: A number of experimental applications of laser cooling of neutral atoms are described. In an experiment on atomic fountains, laser-cooled atoms pushed up on a vertical trajectory by radiation pressure were observed to turn around due to gravity. A compact cesium fountain that would give three to four orders of magnitude increase in the counting rate over the first experiment can be designed, and the trapping and cooling can be done with diode lasers, suggesting a practical clock. In order to increase the time-averaged flux of such a fountain and also create a continuous fountain, an atomic funnel that can produce an atomic beam of very low velocity ( approximately 270 cm/s) at densities of 10/sup 8/ atoms/cm/sup 2/ has been devised.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The establishment of 10 kV to 500/ square root 3 kV power frequency voltage ratio national standard system and study of the calibration method
abstract: Summary form only given. Methods used to establish and calibrate a 10-500/ square root 3 kV power frequency voltage ratio standard system are described. The standards are a series of capacitive dividers. which are calibrated at 6 kV with an inductive voltage divider but used at the higher operating voltages. Four potential transformers, used as 10-, 35-, 110/ square root 3-, and 220/ square root -kV working standards, were calibrated by the new system. Another potential transformer, which had been calibrated at the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) in September/October 1987, was also calibrated with the new system. The results indicate uncertainties of less than 10 parts per million and confirm the comparison with NRC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quantized Hall resistance measurements at KSRI
abstract: The authors describe the system for measuring quantized Hall resistances used at KSRI (Korea Standards Research Institute) and report preliminary results obtained with GaAs-AlGaAs heterostructures. The first result in terms of Omega /sub KSRI/ is: R/sub H4/=6453.2(1+0.36*10/sup -6/+or-0.32 *10/sup -6/) Omega /sub KSRI/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A time-scale algorithm for post-processing: AT1 plus frequency variance
abstract: A time-scale algorithm. AT1 plus frequency variance, run in postprocessed mode is presented. Such a postprocessed scale can take advantage of better characterization of the clocks in the time-scale ensemble and improved capability for frequency step detection. Real and simulated data are used to show how the algorithm compares with AT1 alone.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Abnormal chopping effects on the signal of the metal-insulator metal diode (laser frequency measurement)
abstract: The authors report the experimental results concerning abnormally enhanced effects on the signal detection of point-contact MIM (metal-insulator-metal) diodes when an incident CO/sub 2/ laser beam is chopped at the resonant chopping frequencies with a mechanical chopper. The signal intensity with the chopping effect is about seven times as large as that without the chopping effect. The MIM diode is shown to have a very large S/N (signal/noise ratio) value at the resonant chopping frequencies for the low laser power in the IR regions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The calcium optical frequency standard: present status
abstract: An optical frequency standard based on a dye laser stabilized to the Lamb dip of the Doppler-broadened Ca intercombination line is reported. The measured depth of the Lamb dip depends strongly on the laser power and the excitation geometry and can be explained quantitatively by calculation of the transition probability. The stabilized laser frequency can be made reproducible to better than 300 Hz by stabilizing the same laser to two independent thermal atomic beams with the possibility of laser cooling one of the atomic beams.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Studies of laser-cooled trapped Yb/sup +/ (frequency standard)
abstract: /sup 172/Yb/sup +/ ions in an RF trap have been laser-cooled to 2 K by driving the /sup 2/S/sub 1/2/-/sup 2/P/sub 1/2/ transition at 369.5 nm. Observations of metastable F-state populations at low pressure are reported for large numbers of Yb/sup +/ ions in the trap. A narrow-linewidth ring dye laser for probing an S-D or S-F transition in trapped Yb/sup +/ is considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Realized and planned improvements of the PTBs primary cesium clocks
abstract: Performance data for two primary cesium clocks are reported. Changes that have been made to improve the performance are described. One involves the use of a cavity with ring-shaped end parts in which the atoms interact with the microwave field in a region where its Pointing vector vanishes due to the symmetry. This configuration reduces the distributed phase shift, which seriously interferes with the determination of the end-to-end phase difference of the Ramsey cavity. Other changes involve the C-field correction, electronic system, and figure of instability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The possible role of the fundamental constants in replacing the kilogram
abstract: Summary form only given. The author discusses the possibility of certain fundamental physical constants replacing the current unit of mass in the International System of Units. These constants include the Rydberg, fine-structure, Josephson, and von Klitzing constants, the atomic mass of the proton, and the proton-electron mass ratio.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel audio-frequency compensation circuit for precision measurement
abstract: A novel frequency compensation circuit which may be used for precision measurement is proposed. This circuit can reduce the residual error at audio frequency. A formula for maximum residual error is derived and studied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experimental study of the voltage coefficient of precise compressed-gas capacitors
abstract: A study of the voltage coefficient of precise compressed-gas capacitors is described. A series of measuring methods based on the formula for calculating the voltage coefficient is presented. The following methods were used: measuring the variations of capacitance when the capacitor is tilted in various directions to a specific angle; measuring the variations in capacitance when the capacitor is tilted in a specific direction to various angles; and measuring the variations in the coordinates of the electrodes when these electrodes are subjected to various mechanical forces. These methods were used to test a BF350-50T capacitor, and its voltage coefficient was found to be less than one part in a million from 0 kV up to 350 kV.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An application of GPS dual frequency codeless receiver for ionospheric delay to single frequency VLBI observation
abstract: A dual-frequency codeless Global Positioning System (GPS) receiver for measuring ionospheric delay, called GTR-2, has been developed. Results of a feasibility study of using GTR-2 for single-frequency very-long-baseline interferometry (VLBI) experiments are presented. GTR-2 uses a cross-correlation property of the P-code signals transmitted from GPS satellites to measure ionospheric total electron content (TEC) with a measurement uncertainty of about 2*10/sup 16/ electrons/m/sup 2/ along the line of site to the satellite. Ionospheric compensation of the signal from radio stars is studied using the TEC data obtained from GTR-2.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Feasibility of end to end phase shift correction from the outside of sealed cesium beam tubes (frequency standard)
abstract: Summary from only given. Frequency shift traceable to asymmetry of the microwave resonator occurring in atomic beam frequency standards making use of Ramsey's double interaction technique was addressed. The shift is due to the phase difference that appears between the fields interacting with the atoms in the two regions. Correcting the arm asymmetry by introducing a compensating asymmetry in the symmetric arm of the feeding T-junction was proposed. Electromagnetic calculations of the asymmetry introduced in an E-plane waveguide T-junction by an asymmetric iris in the feeding port were carried out and compared with experimental results. It was found that compensation of end-to-end phase shift is possible in this way, and that shifts of a few parts in 10/sup 13/ can be reduced to below 1*10/sup -13/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 1.5 mu m absolutely stabilized extended-cavity semiconductor laser
abstract: Summary form only given. A compact source (2-L volume) with a stable extended-cavity laser set at 1514 nm but electrically tunable over 0.3 nm using a PZT has been designed and operated as an optical reference frequency. The package also includes an NH/sub 3/ absorption cell providing several strong absorption lines, which are used to frequency-lock the laser on the side of the lines using a static loop in order to avoid residual laser frequency modulation. The frequency stability has been tested using an heterodyne beat between two identical sources. and a 10/sup -10/ relative frequency stability has been measured on a 100-s observation time. For longer observation times, some drifts unavoidable with such a stabilization method are observed: however, it has been shown that the laser frequency could stay in a +or-2-MHz range for several days, which is enough for system requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Determination of scattering parameters with respect to the characteristic impedance of precision coaxial air-line standards (network analysers)
abstract: Scattering parameter expressions with respect to the characteristic impedances corresponding to the principal mode are developed for the coaxial air-line standard. Dimensional variations of the inner and outer conductors and skin-effect loss are included in the model. The local characteristic impedance, which is found from the stored energy principle, is derived from the forward and backward voltage and current waves of the principal mode. Four sources of error for mod S/sub 11/ mod are discussed. Modeling accuracy for the scattering parameters and characteristic impedance is shown to be primarily dependent on conductor radius measurement precision.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple method for separating dissipation factors in microwave printed circuit board
abstract: A simple method for separating the dissipation factors associated with conductor losses and dielectric losses of printed circuit boards in microwave frequencies is presented. The method utilizes the difference in dependence of the two losses on the dimensions of bounded stripline resonators using one printed circuit board specimen as a center strip conductor. The experimental results show that the method is very practical for evaluating loss characteristics in microwave applications. Although separation was achieved under the condition that the permittivity of the substrate was known, it may be possible without knowing the permittivity if the dependence of the fringing capacitance at the resonator ends is measured separately.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Error analysis of scanner in automated inductance calibration system
abstract: An error analysis method for the scanner in an automated inductance calibration system is described. The system is composed of a digital bridge, a scanner, and a personal computer. The random error of values measured with the scanner is compared for the case without a scanner. The influence of the scanning system is explained by a specified model, and the error caused is estimated from two equations derived from this model. At 1 kHz, the system's accuracy is best at 100 mH and decreases either with larger inductance or smaller inductance. This method can also be applied to other automated measurement systems using scanners.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Determination of the volt with the improved PTB voltage balance
abstract: Determinations of the conversion factor of the volt have been carried out after significant improvements to the measuring system. The mean value of 48 determinations was K/sub V/=1-0.02*10/sup -6/, with a standard deviation of the mean s/sub m/=0.064*10/sup -6/. The corresponding frequency-to-voltage quotient is K/sub J/=483597.91 GHz/V. The relative type B uncertainty of the experiment was estimated to be u=0.33*10/sup -6/. These data are preliminary, in as much as the recalibration of the standards used for the capacitance, the mass, and the displacement in terms of the SI units farad, kilogram, and meters had not yet been carried out.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent activities at BIPM in the field of stabilized lasers: radiations recommended for the definition of the metre
abstract: The results of interconnectional comparisons of iodine-stabilized He-Ne lasers at lambda =633 nm between Bureau International des Poids et Mesures (BIPM) and 11 national laboratories are presented. The measured frequency differences were all within +or-3 parts in 10/sup 11/. Investigations concerning He-Ne lasers at lambda =612 nm using internal or external iodine cells are discussed. The frequency reproducibility is limited by, among other things the quality of the iodine cells. Therefore, the contamination of iodine cells has been studied using laser-induced fluorescence. First results obtained on the green line of He-Ne at lambda =543 nm stabilized on iodine are presented. The frequency repeatability between two such systems was (14+or-5) kHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improvements for automating voltage calibrations using a 10-V Josephson array
abstract: Three changes that were introduced to automate totally a voltage standard system based on a 10-V Josephson array are described. A commercial standard cell scanner controls switching for calibrating either Zener references or digital voltmeters, a programmable attenuator helps in obtaining voltage steps, and measurements of digital voltmeter noise help in verifying array stability. The array system operates completely unattended.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The measurement of equivalent source match
abstract: A fast and accurate swept frequency method of measuring source match is introduced. It is demonstrated that it is possible to measure the S/sub g/ of a leveled source using a vector network analyzer. A detailed error analysis has been done for the measurement of the source match of a resistive power splitter using an HP8510B network analyzer. The mean difference between this system and the traditional slotted line/sliding short method is less than +or-0.01 voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) units. The method thus shows no systematic error.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A transportable voltage standard based on a mercury battery
abstract: The NPL (National Physical Laboratory, United Kingdom) moving-coil measurements need a portable voltage source stable to 1 in 10/sup 9/ for a day to relate the results to a Josephson array voltage standard. A carefully-thermostated 1.35-V mercury cell has been shown to be superior to both Zener diodes and Weston cells if its decreasing voltage of about 0.3 mu V/h is compensated by a series voltage increasing at an equal and opposite rate. The nonlinearity with time of the compensation voltage is less than three in 10/sup 5/ of its maximum output, and the resulting nonlinearity of the total voltage from this cause is less than one in 10/sup 9/. The total RMS voltage noise in a 1-Hz bandwidth is less than 1 nV, and the isolation of all internal circuitry from the case is about 10/sup 11/ Omega . It is pointed out that this device could be more generally applicable as a transportable voltage standard.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Predictions of antenna performances from near field measurements at micro- and mm-wave frequencies
abstract: The problems associated with accurate predictions of antenna performances at microwave and millimeter-wave frequencies are studied. A number of possible techniques that have been proposed for pattern predictions at millimeter-wave frequencies are described. The viability of the techniques has been studied theoretically and experimentally. The results demonstrate the suitability of the techniques for predicting the performance of antennas in the millimeter-wave regime.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Compensation of mismatch between magnetic characteristics of DC comparators
abstract: Results of a detailed analysis of the errors resulting from mismatch between the dynamic magnetic characteristics of DC comparators are presented, and a way to reduce them is discussed. A modification of the comparator circuit is proposed to minimize the influence of core mismatch on the comparator operating characteristics. The proposed compensation circuit is shown to be effective in improving the operating characteristics of the DC comparator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Josephson voltage standard using a biharmonic drive
abstract: A novel approach to a Josephson voltage standard is presented. It uses as the drive signal the combination of a 10-GHz signal and its second harmonic. The effect of this biharmonic drive is to enhance the constant-voltage step amplitudes with respect to those obtained with a single-frequency drive. The optimum operating conditions are discussed, and the first experimental results obtained with Josephson devices containing both single junctions and small arrays are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CuGeMn a new material for high precision cryo-resistors
abstract: The electrical resistance of CuGeMn alloys was measured as a function of temperature. It shows maxima at temperatures between 1.5 K and 9.1 K. Since the temperature coefficient at the maxima is zero and since the resistivity is high, these alloys are very suitable for the construction of cryo-resistors which are operated in liquid helium and can be used to improve quantum Hall measurement systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigations into the deflection of relativistic electrons inside a superconducting cavity resonator for measuring high voltages
abstract: An electron speed filtering system with a superconducting cavity resonator was investigated in order to check its applicability to precise high-voltage measurements. Extensive theoretical and experimental work has been performed. Numerical calculations of the motion of relativistic electrons have shown a dependence of calibration voltages on the electromagnetic field strength. A discrepancy between theoretical and experimental calibration voltages was also observed. Despite good reproducibility, the calibration points observed do not therefore allow a precise high-voltage scale to be built.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A VLF voltage standard from 0.01 to 50 Hz
abstract: A voltage standard for the range from 0.01 to 50 Hz is presented. It consists of a sampling very-low-frequency (VLF) root mean square (RMS) voltmeter and a VLF voltage calibrator which provides a high-accuracy and high-stability sine waveform, with ranges of 10 mV, 100 mV, 1 V, and 10 V. The accuracy of the calibrator is better than +or-300 p.p.m. and that of the voltmeter is better than +or-0.1% above 10 mV. The VLF voltage standard can be used to calibrate other voltmeters and voltage sources.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The establishment of an independent impedance standard at KSRI
abstract: The construction of 100 and 1000-pF hermetically sealed gas-dielectric capacitors. a 1-k Omega AC/DC transfer resistor. and 10- and 100-k Omega AC resistors to be used as impedance elements of a quadrature bridge is described. Their electrical properties as measured by single- and two-stage ratio transformer bridges are reported. The results are preliminary.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automated voltage divider to calibrate a 10-V output of Zener voltage standard
abstract: The authors present a voltage divider developed to calibrate the 10-V output of a Zener-diode voltage standard with reference to a 1-V Josephson array voltage standard. The ratio of the divider can be automatically self-calibrated by a digital voltmeter and a switching system controlled by a computer. The principle used for ratio calibration of the voltage divider is discussed. The configuration used for measurement of the divider ratio and the configuration used for calibration of the 10-V output of the Zener standard are described. The operation of the system is also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Direct comparisons of quantized Hall resistances
abstract: The quantized Hall resistances (QHRs) of three GaAs/Al/sub x/Ga/sub 1-x/As heterostructures were directly compared. Two of the three samples were grown by metalorganic chemical vapor deposition. and the third was produced by molecular beam epitaxy. A cryogenic current comparator bridge was used for the measurements. The provisional results show a residual difference lower than a few parts in 10/sup 9/ with an uncertainty of the same order.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel algorithm for precision RMS measurement of VLF voltage
abstract: Summary form only given. A novel algorithm for precision RMS (root mean square) measurement of VLF voltage is presented. The final result of the measured signal, including RMS value and frequency, can be obtained via successive approximation by the least-squares method, an optimization technique, and other special means. The objective function is the sampled data string of the measured signal.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: DC-SQUID based displacement sensor for a Mossbauer red-shift experiment
abstract: A superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID)-based displacement sensor with resolution up to 3*10/sup -15/ m/ square root Hz in the frequency band of 20 Hz-15 kHz is reported. The sensor monitors the Doppler modulation of gamma radiation in a gravitational red-shift experiment using the 93-keV Mossbauer resonance of /sup 67/Zn. Test results for the SQUID and the PZT transducer used in the experiment are presented. The relative statistical uncertainty in the determination of the gravitational red shift is about 3% for a one-week experiment. Preliminary results obtained with the displacement sensor show that the systematic uncertainties that are related to the Doppler motion generated by the velocity drive are negligible compared to the statistical uncertainty.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement of ferrites tensor permeability by spherical cavity resonator
abstract: The authors describe the measurement of the microwave tensor permeability of a ferrite biased with a DC-magnetic field using a spherical cavity resonator. The principle of measurement, a practical spherical cavity, the measurement system, and the measurement results on YIG ferrite at 10 GHz are presented. The Q value of the spherical cavity is shown to be about 1.5-2 times higher than that of the rectangular or circular cavity resonator, making this cavity appropriate for precise measurements. Exact solutions can be obtained using this method. Using a spherical ferrite sample, the internal H/sub DC/ field is uniform and can be exactly calculated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The Danish Josephson array voltage calibration system
abstract: The Danish system for calibration of DC voltages up to 10 V is described. Emphasis is on the design and verification of the Josephson array setup and the certified scheme based on Zener references for dissemination of traceability to industry. To correct for offset and linear drift, three null measurements and two array voltage reversals are used in the calibration procedure. The uncorrected thermal voltages and drift originating mainly from the switch box are estimated to be about 1 nV. Calibration of the 10-V terminals is done by means of a high-linearity voltmeter. The nonlinearity of the voltmeter is the major source of error in the method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High T/sub c/ RF-SQUID galvanometer
abstract: A high-T/sub c/ superconducting galvanometer with a sensitivity of 2*10/sup -12/ A/ square root Hz for input resistance of 250 Omega is reported. Its sensor is a YBaCuO RF SQUID (superconducting quantum interference device) that operates at 77 K. In the absence of high-T/sub c/ superconducting wires, this RF SQUID solves the problem of coupling between the signal and SQUID ring very well.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of the quantized Hall resistance in different GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures
abstract: GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures with mobilities varying between 15 and 50 T/sup -1/ have been successfully fabricated and contacted. The quantized Hall resistances of seven different samples have been compared with an uncertainty of less than 1 part in 10/sup 8/ using a potentiometric measurement system. Preliminary results for the relative differences of the QHR measured on three different GaAs samples are shown. No sample dependence has been found at a precision level of 1 part in 10/sup 8/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A digital three-phase watthour meter
abstract: A microprocessor-controlled three-phase digital watthour meter is described. The wattmeter is based on a sampling method and on an analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion; only one 10-b A/D converter, integrated in a microprocessor, is used. The resolution of the converter is improved by superimposing noise on current and voltage signals, and its uncertainty is reduced via an external resistive voltage divider. A wide current range is achieved by passing voltage signals. proportional to input currents, through a programmable-gain amplifier. The overall uncertainty of the meter is less than 0.1%. A block diagram of the wattmeter is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Alternative methods for relating electrical to mechanical quantities through power equation
abstract: The problem of linking mechanical quantities with electrical ones measured in terms of the time unit, the electron charge, and the Planck constant is considered. Some methods based on dynamic voltage devices are presented in principle, as alternatives to methods for SI watt determination based on moving-coil current balances. Three possible approaches to the problem, based on voltage devices and leading to power equations, are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microwave directional coupler design using spectral domain technique
abstract: A systematic algorithm for selecting the basis function for microwave directional couplers is presented. It is shown that microwave directional couplers can be grouped under four major categories: simple configurations, such as broadside-coupled suspended substrate stripline structure, broadside-coupled strip with overlay, and coupled suspended lines with septum; more complex configurations, such as edge-coupled strips with overlay; structures involving anisotropic material such as coupled microstrip on double anisotropic substrate layers; and asymmetric structures such as broadside-coupled striplines of unequal width. For each category, there exists an optimal basis function: one-term quadratic function; two-term quadratic function; logarithmic function; and Chebyschev function weighted by an edge condition.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
